narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>The dog leaps nine feet each time. One hundred and fifty divided by nine is seventeen leaps.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But after seventeen leaps the rabbit has run on, and the gap is still there.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The whole leap does not close the gap, so that slip is struck.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Find the gain in one leap, then divide the head start by the gain.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>To check, work out the distance each animal has run.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Both distances should match when the dog catches up.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words find the gain in one leap and divide the head start by it appear; the two equal distances are shown with a tick

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip divides the head start by the dog's leap alone and gets about seventeen leaps. The rabbit keeps running, so the dog must cover the gap by its gain only.
